architecture_summary: A fully local, GPU-accelerated soccer foul detection pipeline: OpenCV extracts 16 evenly-spaced RGB frames from the input clip; CLIP (openai/clip-vit-base-patch32) zero-shot heads detect player contact and penalty-box location; VideoMAE (MCG-NJU/videomae-base-finetuned-kinetics) classifies foul type via a Kinetics-to-foul label mapping; dense Farneback optical flow drives a deterministic severity heuristic; and a pure-Python IFAB-style ruling engine combines all signals into a final punishment ruling with confidence. Every ML module caches its model as a module-level singleton and exposes a MODEL_ID string constant at the top of the file as the swap hook for fine-tuned replacements.

public_api.frame_extractor.py: extract_frames(video_path: str, num_frames: int = 16) -> tuple[list[np.ndarray], list[float]]  # RGB uint8 HxWx3 frames, timestamps in seconds
public_api.foul_classifier.py: classify_foul(frames: list[np.ndarray]) -> dict  # {"foul_type": str one of tackle|handball|obstruction|simulation|push|none, "confidence": float}
public_api.severity_assessor.py: assess_severity(frames: list[np.ndarray], foul_type: str) -> dict  # {"severity": str one of careless|reckless|excessive_force, "confidence": float, "peak_motion": float}
public_api.ruling_engine.py: make_ruling(contact: dict, foul: dict, severity: dict, location: dict) -> dict  # {"foul_detected": bool, "foul_type": str, "severity": str, "in_penalty_box": bool, "punishment": str, "confidence": float}
public_api.pipeline.py: run_pipeline(video_path: str, num_frames: int = 16) -> dict  # final ruling dict; also a CLI: python pipeline.py clip.mp4

modules.outputs: frames: list[np.ndarray] (RGB uint8 HxWx3), timestamps: list[float] (seconds)
key_decisions: Sample num_frames evenly spaced by frame index across the full clip using cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT
Convert BGR to RGB before returning so downstream HuggingFace processors get RGB
If a frame read fails (corrupt frame), reuse the last successfully decoded frame and continue; raise ValueError only if zero frames decode
Raise FileNotFoundError for a missing video path with a clear message
Timestamps computed from frame index / fps, falling back to index-based estimates when fps metadata is missing
modules.swap_hook_description: No ML model, but include a SWAP HOOK comment block explaining how to replace uniform sampling with a learned keyframe selector (e.g., a fine-tuned action-proposal model) by reimplementing the frame-index selection function.

key_decisions: Zero-shot CLIP with contrastive text prompts: positive prompts describe two soccer players in physical contact / colliding / tackling, negative prompts describe players running with no contact
Score every frame, take the max positive-prompt softmax probability across frames as the contact confidence (contact is momentary, so max not mean)
contact = confidence >= 0.5
Model + processor cached as module-level singletons loaded on first call, moved to cuda if available with graceful CPU fallback
modules.swap_hook_description: MODEL_ID = "openai/clip-vit-base-patch32" string constant at top of file; SWAP HOOK comment shows changing it to a fine-tuned checkpoint (e.g., your-org/clip-soccer-contact) and notes that prompt lists can also be tuned.

key_decisions: VideoMAE expects exactly 16 frames; pad by repeating the last frame or subsample evenly if given a different count

Pre-trained head outputs Kinetics-400 action labels, not foul types: map top-k predicted Kinetics labels to foul types via a keyword mapping dict (e.g., labels containing 'tackl' -> tackle, 'wrestling'/'push' -> push, 'juggling soccer ball'/'kicking' with low motion -> none), defaulting to 'none' when no mapped label appears in top-5
Return the softmax probability mass of the winning mapped label group as confidence
This mapping is explicitly a stopgap: the real accuracy comes from the SoccerNet fine-tune described in the swap hook
modules.swap_hook_description: MODEL_ID = "MCG-NJU/videomae-base-finetuned-kinetics" constant at top; SWAP HOOK comment block shows switching to a SoccerNet fine-tuned checkpoint with a direct 6-class head (tackle/handball/obstruction/simulation/push/none) and deleting the Kinetics keyword-mapping function.

modules.model: none — OpenCV Farneback dense optical flow
key_decisions: Compute dense Farneback optical flow between consecutive grayscale frame pairs (downscaled to width 320 for speed); severity signal = peak of the 95th-percentile flow magnitude across pairs, normalized by frame diagonal
Thresholds on normalized peak motion: < 0.010 -> careless, 0.010–0.025 -> reckless, > 0.025 -> excessive_force
Foul-type-aware overrides: simulation is always careless (no real contact); handball capped at reckless (severity of handball is about denial, not force)
Confidence derived from distance of the motion value from the nearest threshold boundary (values near a boundary get ~0.5, far from boundaries approach 0.9)
modules.swap_hook_description: SWAP HOOK comment block shows replacing the heuristic with a fine-tuned video regression/classification model: add MODEL_ID constant (placeholder string provided, e.g. "your-org/videomae-severity"), and reimplement assess_severity to call it, keeping the same return dict.

key_decisions: Zero-shot CLIP with contrastive prompts: positive prompts describe play inside the penalty area near the goal with the goalkeeper and penalty-box lines visible, negative prompts describe midfield play far from goal
Use the middle 50% of frames (the foul moment) and average the positive-prompt softmax probability (location is stable across the incident, so mean not max)
in_penalty_box = confidence >= 0.5
Loads its own CLIP singleton independently of contact_detector so each module file is fully self-contained (HuggingFace disk cache makes the second load cheap; both fit in the VRAM budget)
modules.swap_hook_description: MODEL_ID = "openai/clip-vit-base-patch32" constant at top; SWAP HOOK comment shows swapping to a fine-tuned pitch-localization model (e.g., a keypoint/homography model trained on SoccerNet-calibration) while keeping the same return dict.

modules.model: none — pure Python rule logic, deterministic, no ML imports
modules.inputs: contact: dict, foul: dict, severity: dict, location: dict (the outputs of the four upstream modules)
modules.outputs: {"foul_detected": bool, "foul_type": str, "severity": str, "in_penalty_box": bool, "punishment": str, "confidence": float}
key_decisions: foul_detected = (foul_type != 'none') AND (contact OR foul_type in {handball, simulation}) — handball and simulation do not require player-to-player contact
IFAB-style punishment mapping: careless -> 'free kick'; reckless -> 'free kick + yellow card'; excessive_force -> 'free kick + red card'; simulation -> 'free kick + yellow card (simulation)'
If in_penalty_box and foul_detected and foul_type != simulation: replace 'free kick' with 'penalty kick' in the punishment string; excessive force in the box -> 'penalty kick + red card'
If no foul: punishment = 'play on', foul_type = 'none', severity passed through as 'careless' floor
Overall confidence = geometric mean of the confidences of the modules that actually contributed to the decision
Zero ML imports — only stdlib (math) — so this file is trivially unit-testable
modules.swap_hook_description: SWAP HOOK comment block explains this module is intentionally NOT swappable for a model: rules stay deterministic and auditable; to change behavior, edit the PUNISHMENT_TABLE dict constant.

modules.inputs: video_path: str (CLI argument), num_frames: int = 16 (--num-frames flag)
modules.outputs: final ruling dict printed as pretty JSON to stdout; run_pipeline() also returns it
key_decisions: Imports the five sibling modules directly (from frame_extractor import extract_frames, etc.) and calls them in sequence: extract -> contact -> foul -> severity -> location -> ruling
Sequential execution (not parallel) to bound peak VRAM to one model's activations at a time; models stay resident as singletons
argparse CLI: python pipeline.py clip.mp4 [--num-frames 16]; exits with code 1 and a readable message on missing/corrupt video
Prints per-stage progress lines to stderr and only the final JSON dict to stdout so output is pipeable
Adds the directory containing pipeline.py to sys.path so it works when invoked from any cwd
modules.swap_hook_description: SWAP HOOK comment block notes that stages are swapped inside each module file (via their MODEL_ID constants), not here; the orchestrator only depends on the public function signatures listed in the architecture plan.

key_decisions: torch installed separately via the CUDA 11.8 index URL (comment at top of file)
Pin transformers, opencv-python, numpy, Pillow, decord, accelerate to versions stable as of mid-2025
